svg.title: Submetacentric chromosome movement
svg.desc: Two sequential views of one cell, schematic and not measured to scale. At metaphase, one replicated submetacentric chromosome has two continuous sister chromatids joined at their paired centromeric units. Opposite poles attach to the outward-facing unit of each sister. At anaphase, two single daughter chromosomes separate in the same cell: their centromeres lead toward opposite poles, and their long upper and short lower arms trail as mirrored J shapes opening toward the middle.
